Timeline::is_friday¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::is_friday() const

Aliases: fri_is() and is_fri().

Select Local Fridays¶

is_friday() marks every timestamp whose local date is Friday. The output is a shape-preserving boolean Series; NaT becomes false.

Example¶

const auto week = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-03-04T12:00:00Z", "2024-03-05T12:00:00Z",
    "2024-03-06T12:00:00Z", "2024-03-07T12:00:00Z",
    "2024-03-08T12:00:00Z", "2024-03-09T12:00:00Z",
    "2024-03-10T12:00:00Z", "",
});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, week.is_friday());

Output¶

Series(shape=[8], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[false, false, false, false, true, false, false, false]

Friday is the final true under the built-in Monday-Friday business-day rule. That does not imply it is an open day for a particular market, country, or organization; holiday policy remains external.

Combining Friday With Other Rules¶

A rule such as “Friday and month end” can be expressed by combining this mask with is_month_end(). Each predicate describes calendar membership, so their intersection remains elementwise and shape-aligned.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Friday is not treated as a weekend.

  • false can mean another weekday or NaT.

  • A timezone change near midnight can alter the result.
